title: benchmarks.py pool verify checks a record's consistency, and a capped smoke record passes it
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py pool verify [--file F] [--record R] exits 1, naming each, when a pool record breaks one of: every arm label the run planned has rows for all kinds it ran; each run's cost is within 20% of the list-price cost of its counted tokens (bench_core.PRICE), which catches a cumulative session cost and an output undercount; a label's spend rows equal the sum of its runs' costs; no position of a session label has a mean cost rising with position; out is above zero on every model arm; errors are under 2% of runs; it exits 0 otherwise, and a test plants each break. Then the smoke record: the orchestrator runs the record's one command (all arms with the Opus arm, both shapes, --sample 2 rows per kind, 1 rep, --jobs 8, --max-usd 25, at most 25 USD: the operator's answer to g7 over the dry-run's estimate of about 23 USD) with --out into the scratch directory, never benchmarks.csv, and pool verify on that file exits 0; a defect the smoke shows is filed as an S1 bug in this sprint and fixed before this story is done. kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md's pool section states the record procedure: the one command, its cap, the smoke first, then verify

gates.question: Which inputs does pool verify read?
options: The results file only: the record writes each run figure verify needs (planned kinds, off-list run count, list cost, cost per session position) as rows
The results file and the record's runs file, found by the record date in the scratch directory
gates.recommendation: The results file only: the record writes each run figure verify needs (planned kinds, off-list run count, list cost, cost per session position) as rows
gates.answer: The results file only: the record writes each run figure verify needs (planned kinds, off-list run count, list cost, cost per session position) as rows

gates.question: How does a position's mean cost count as rising in a session label?
options: The mean cost is higher at every position than at the one before, over 3 or more positions
The mean cost of the last position is over 1.5 times that of the first
gates.recommendation: The mean cost is higher at every position than at the one before, over 3 or more positions
gates.answer: The mean cost is higher at every position than at the one before, over 3 or more positions

gates.question: How does verify treat the record of 2026-10-08, which predates the figures verify reads?
options: As a past record: the properties its rows cannot carry (the planned kinds, the list price of a run, the cost per position) are named in a note and not checked, the others are checked; a record with planned kinds rows is checked in full
Not at all: the check on it is dropped from the item
gates.recommendation: As a past record: the properties its rows cannot carry (the planned kinds, the list price of a run, the cost per position) are named in a note and not checked, the others are checked; a record with planned kinds rows is checked in full
gates.answer: As a past record: the properties its rows cannot carry (the planned kinds, the list price of a run, the cost per position) are named in a note and not checked, the others are checked; a record with planned kinds rows is checked in full

gates.question: Which share of runs may fail, and over what?
options: Under 2% of all the record's runs together, a label with no counted output caught by its own property
Under 2% of each arm label's runs
gates.recommendation: Under 2% of all the record's runs together, a label with no counted output caught by its own property
gates.answer: Under 2% of all the record's runs together, a label with no counted output caught by its own property

gates.question: How many runs may cost more than 20% from the list price of their counted input and output?
options: None: every run of a model arm is within 20%
A share of the runs up to the failed-run share of 2%
gates.recommendation: None: every run of a model arm is within 20%
gates.answer: None: every run of a model arm is within 20%

gates.question: At which price does the list cost of a run count its cache writes?
options: Twice the input price (the 1-hour write the runs are billed at, agent-caching.md line 23), in the record's list cost and in the dry-run estimate
The 5-minute write price of bench_core.PRICE, the runs' cost then reading 1.5 to 2 times the list cost on a Sonnet 5.5 lookup
gates.recommendation: Twice the input price (the 1-hour write the runs are billed at, agent-caching.md line 23), in the record's list cost and in the dry-run estimate
gates.answer: each cache write at its own TTL from the usage's per-TTL split, else the billing surface's default (a subscription's 1-hour rate), one rule in bench_core (changed in the review: BG-6e7lim27 implements it)

gates.question: Which --max-usd does the smoke carry, as the dry-run's estimate for the goal's flags is above 5?
options: 5, as the goal states: the run stops at the cap, exits 1 and verify names its spend_stopped rows
A cap above the dry-run's estimate of the same flags, so every arm label and both shapes run
gates.recommendation: A cap above the dry-run's estimate of the same flags, so every arm label and both shapes run
gates.answer: A cap above the dry-run's estimate of the same flags, so every arm label and both shapes run

gates.question: Which flags does the full record carry?
options: The smoke's arms, shapes and --jobs without --sample, at --reps 1, and a --max-usd above the dry-run's estimate
The smoke's flags without --sample and with the per-arm reps of the record of 2026-10-08 (3 for the kb arms, 2 for Sonnet 5.5, the web arms and the sessions)
gates.recommendation: The smoke's arms, shapes and --jobs without --sample, at --reps 1, and a --max-usd above the dry-run's estimate
gates.answer: The smoke's arms, shapes and --jobs without --sample, at --reps 1, and a --max-usd above the dry-run's estimate

notes: Blocks the next pool benchmark record: the operator asked on 2026-10-08 for the work needed before the next record to be staged as SP-2vhfsn4o. The operator wants the record after this sprint to need no further fix sprint, so the smoke record runs the whole command once at a small cost inside this sprint. Premise: pool verify does not exist (the first check exits 2 today); on the 2026-10-08 record it must exit 0 only once that record's spend and session costs are corrected (BG-2tan24sm). --sample is added by the one-command story if it is not there yet; this story may add it. The smoke's paid runs are the orchestrator's (a worker's foreground command has a 10-minute limit): the brief names the command and the worker writes verify and the test. Smoke 1, 2026-10-08: --max-usd 25 stopped after 246 paid runs at 26.62 USD (Opus 15.7 against 7.84 estimated); router, hook, web and session labels never started; pool verify exit 1 on (a) the stopped labels and (b) six off-list runs. Filed BG-rbokisbc and BG-kwxzwsfd (S1). The operator approved a second smoke at --max-usd 40 after both fixes. Smoke 2, 2026-10-09: all 15 labels ran, 35.00 USD; verify (b) failed the session labels on running output totals (BG-xbxtbqwd). Smoke 3: all labels ran, 34.43 USD; verify (b) failed the Sonnet 5.5 session and web labels on the cache read price (BG-pv3hl6aa). The operator raised the session's spend approval to 300 USD and left it unattended.
